extra.message: The 'user_pic' view reads a file using a filename taken directly from request.GET.get('p') and joins it into a base path with os.path.join without any sanitization. Because os.path.join with an absolute path or '../' sequences escapes the intended base directory, an attacker can read arbitrary files on the server (e.g. ?p=../../../../etc/passwd). This is a path traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The 'code_execution' view passes user-supplied input (request.POST['first_name'], base64-decoded) directly to exec(). This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary Python code on the server, leading to full remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Fallback path in 'code_execution' passes user-supplied base64-decoded request.POST['first_name'] directly to exec() (Python 2 path), allowing arbitrary Python code execution / remote code execution.

extra.message: The 'unvalidated_redirect' view passes a user-controlled value from request.GET.get('url') directly to django redirect() without validating that it points to a trusted/local destination. An attacker can craft a link that redirects victims to an arbitrary external site (phishing). This is an open redirect.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The 'unvalidated_forward' view uses a user-supplied value (request.GET.get('fwd')) to look up and invoke a function from globals() with the request object. An attacker can invoke arbitrary module-level callables (an unvalidated forward), bypassing intended access controls and reaching views/functions that were not meant to be exposed.

This results in reflected Cross-Site Scripting where attacker-supplied query input is executed as JavaScript.

extra.message: The 'xss_form' view takes request.GET.get('qs') and renders it via vulnerable/xss/form.html using the |safe filter ({{qs|safe}}) in an input value attribute, disabling auto-escaping. This is reflected Cross-Site Scripting allowing arbitrary HTML/JS injection.

extra.message: The 'dor_user_profile' view returns and updates user records based solely on the 'userid' value taken from the URL, with no authentication or authorization check. Any user can view or modify any other user's profile (name/email) by changing the userid, including the admin account. This is an Insecure Direct Object Reference / broken access control.

extra.message: The 'missing_access_control' view renders an admin page based solely on the request parameter action=admin, with no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can access admin functionality simply by supplying ?action=admin. This is a missing function-level access control vulnerability.

The 'csrf_image' view is decorated with @csrf_exempt, disabling Django's CSRF protection for this endpoint and reflecting a user-supplied 'qs' parameter. Combined with globally disabled CSRF middleware, this exposes the application to Cross-Site Request Forgery.

The Django CsrfViewMiddleware is commented out in MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, globally disabling CSRF protection for the entire application. All POST forms (e.g. SQL, code-execution, profile update) are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery.

DEBUG is set to True. In a deployed Django application this exposes detailed stack traces, settings, SQL queries and other sensitive internal information to anyone who triggers an error (e.g. the /misconfiguration/boom endpoint), leading to sensitive information disclosure.

The Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source code. Knowledge of the SECRET_KEY allows an attacker to forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, password-reset tokens and signed data, leading to authentication bypass and tampering.

The 'boom' view deliberately raises an unhandled exception. With DEBUG=True this returns a full Django debug page exposing source code, settings and environment details to the client, resulting in sensitive information disclosure.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
